items.name: accordion
items.title: Accordion
items.description: A stack of collapsible sections — single or multiple open, animated height, a rotating chevron, full keyboard support.

meta.whenToUse: Group related content into collapsible sections — FAQs, settings groups.
meta.whenNotToUse: Hiding critical content, or sequential steps (stepper).

items.name: action-bar
items.title: Action Bar
items.description: Floating contextual bar — status region + action children, CSS-only enter/exit, raised band. Bulk selection, unsaved changes, and batch progress are recipes over it.

meta.whenToUse: A floating bar of contextual actions tied to transient state — N selected, unsaved changes, a batch operation in flight. The host owns the state; the bar shows status and actions.
meta.whenNotToUse: Transient outcome notifications (toast), page-level primary actions (PageHeader), or owning selection — the host's list keeps selectedIds.

items.name: alert
items.title: Alert
items.description: A status banner — upstream's two variants plus our three extra status tones (COL-12); buttons inside a status alert hover in the family's own tint and ink, never white.

meta.whenToUse: Persistent, in-page status messages — info, success, warning, or error context tied to surrounding content.
meta.whenNotToUse: Transient feedback after a user action — use a toast instead.

items.name: alert-dialog
items.title: Alert Dialog
items.description: A modal that interrupts for a decision — media slot, two sizes, and an action/cancel footer.

meta.whenToUse: A decision that must be made before anything else continues — deleting, discarding, signing out.
meta.whenNotToUse: Anything dismissible by clicking away, or a form — use a Dialog.

items.name: shell-layout
items.title: Shell Layout
items.description: The shell's layout rule as one pure function — resolveShellLayout decides, for a width, whether the rail shows and whether the column takes room or slides over — plus the shell's sizes, the column cookie and its width clamp.

meta.whenToUse: Code that must know where the shell puts the column without a DOM — a server render, a test, a docs table — or the shell's sizes and cookie format.
meta.whenNotToUse: Laying the shell out: Shell does that in CSS before hydration; read the live outcome with useShellLayout.

items.name: shell
items.title: Shell
items.description: The frame every screen sits in — a 44px global bar across the top, then a 64px module rail, the module's resizable column, the page under its 48px top bar with fixed slots, and a phone bottom bar — laid out in CSS before hydration, with the cookie state script and the floating area.

meta.whenToUse: The app's frame: the global bar, the rail of modules, a module's column, the page's top bar and the page, on every width from a 320px phone to a wide desktop window, in the browser and the desktop app.
meta.whenNotToUse: Sign-in, public and marketing pages (no shell), or a region inside a page (use a grid or ResizablePanelGroup).

items.name: nav-tree
items.title: Nav Tree
items.description: A column's navigation: titled sections of items left-aligned with their title, children indented one 12px step under their parent, counts, an inset rounded active state, a fold control at a parent's end, arrow-key navigation and a 44px touch size.

meta.whenToUse: The places in an app's module column — views, saved filters, spaces with their sections, folders, settings pages — in the shell's ShellColumn or a phone sheet.
meta.whenNotToUse: A file browser with drag and drop (FolderTree), a page's own tabs (Tabs), or the module rail (Rail).

items.name: global-bar
items.title: Global Bar
items.description: The app's 44px bar across the top of every page: leading (column toggle, back and forward, workspace switcher), a centred search trigger with ⌘K, and trailing (Ask with ⌘J, Help, account). It is the desktop app's draggable title row, clears the window's own buttons, and hides on phones.

meta.whenToUse: The shell's top row (Shell's globalBar), in the browser and as the desktop app's title row.
meta.whenNotToUse: A page's own header and actions (ShellTopBar), or a phone's top row.

items.name: rail
items.title: Rail
items.description: The module rail down the app's start edge: about seven modules, each an icon over a short label with a compact count badge or a dot, and a bottom group. Server-rendered; an item's animated icon loads when the browser is idle.

meta.whenToUse: The app's modules in the shell (Shell's rail).
meta.whenNotToUse: A module's own places (NavTree in the column), search, help or the account (the global bar), or a phone (ShellBottomBar).

items.name: document-layout
items.title: Document Layout
items.description: A page read as a document — the title area and its meta lines, a 720px text column, what follows it, a contents rail before it and a comment margin after it — on one grid with five tiers by its own width, plus its skeleton and a tier hook.

meta.whenToUse: A page people read and write as a document (a wiki page, a spec, a public page, a version's full view): the text at a calm measure with a contents list and a comment margin when there is room, and its loading skeleton on the same grid.
meta.whenNotToUse: A record page (RecordLayout), a form or settings page (ShellPage size="form"), or a list.

items.name: peek
items.title: Peek
items.description: A record over the right of the page area without leaving its list; a bottom sheet with snap points on a phone.

meta.whenToUse: Looking at a record from a list, board, table, search result, Inbox or a mention chip, without leaving it: ↑ ↓ walk the list, ⤢ opens the full page.
meta.whenNotToUse: Working on one record — open its page (RecordLayout); a form or a confirmation — Dialog or Sheet.

items.name: record-layout
items.title: Record Layout
items.description: A record page: the main column, and the right-edge strip that opens one reference panel at a time.

meta.whenToUse: A record page (a task, a meeting, a page, a customer): the work in one main column, and its reference material (Details, Transcript, Files, Versions, Activity, Ask) in one side panel opened from the strip.
meta.whenNotToUse: A list page — a row opens in Peek; a page with no record (a dashboard) — use ShellPage alone.

items.name: comments
items.title: Comments
items.description: A record's comments, Linear style: thread cards (first comment, Show N more replies, indented replies over hairlines, a flat reply row with the viewer's avatar), a bordered composer with a toolbar row and file drop, day labels, a list with a count, order toggle, Load earlier, skeleton and empty states, edit/delete/copy link/copy text, emoji reactions and an attachments slot.

meta.whenToUse: Discussion on a record's page (a task, a meeting): Linear-style thread cards (first comment, replies, a flat reply row) with the composer at the end (at the top newest first).
meta.whenNotToUse: An activity feed or notifications — use Inbox.

items.name: activity-feed
items.title: Activity Feed
items.description: A record's history, Linear style: comment threads and activity events ("Priya changed status from Open to Done · 2h") in one list, with an All / Comments / Activity filter, an order toggle, collapsible event groups, a New divider, a floating Jump to latest, J/K/X keyboard navigation and a skeleton.

meta.whenToUse: A record's history on its page (a task, a deal, a document): what changed, who changed it and when, interleaved with the comment threads.
meta.whenNotToUse: Comments alone (Comments), a cross-record notification list (Inbox).

items.name: comment-margin
items.title: Comment Margin
items.description: Comment cards laid beside the text they are about — level with their highlight, stacked without overlap, the active card aligned with its text — and a CommentPopover anchored to a highlight for narrow screens.

meta.whenToUse: Inline comment threads beside a document (TextEdit annotations + onAnnotationsLayout) on wide screens; the popover below the margin breakpoint.
meta.whenNotToUse: A plain comments section under a record (CommentList), or touch-sized screens (Sheet side="bottom").

items.name: version-list
items.title: Version List
items.description: A document's version history — time, author, name, kind badges (Current, Restored, Unsaved copy), a Named only switch and Load more — as a keyboard listbox.

meta.whenToUse: A page's version history beside a DiffView, in a sheet.
meta.whenNotToUse: An activity feed (ActivityFeed) or a list of records (DataList).

items.name: version-compare
items.title: Version Compare
items.description: A document's version history at full size — the selected version (or its changes through DiffView) beside a day-grouped VersionList on resizable panels, with Restore and Copy pinned in a footer; on a phone the list first and the preview pushed in.

meta.whenToUse: A document's full history in DialogContent size="fullscreen": read a version or its changes beside the list, and restore or copy it.
meta.whenNotToUse: A short history beside a page (VersionList alone), an activity feed (ActivityFeed), or comparing two arbitrary texts (DiffView).

items.name: diff-view
items.title: Diff View
items.description: What changed between two texts — changed lines, then the words inside them, removed struck through and added tinted — with the sanctioned diff engine in its own lazily loaded chunk; line-only above 200 KB.

meta.whenToUse: Comparing two versions of a page's Markdown in a version history.
meta.whenNotToUse: Code review with side-by-side hunks, or live change tracking while editing.

items.name: block-view
items.title: Block View
items.description: The frame TextEdit and MarkdownView draw a fenced block in when a blockViews entry renders its language: the label, Preview / Code, a split view on a wide editable block, Expand (a full-screen dialog with pan and pinch) and a ⋯ menu.

meta.whenToUse: Internal to TextEdit and MarkdownView: pass blockViews to either rather than mounting it.
meta.whenNotToUse: Showing code (CodeBlock) or a standalone diagram (MermaidBlock).

items.name: mermaid-block
items.title: Mermaid Block
items.description: A mermaid diagram drawn in the browser — the engine loaded lazily, the configuration pinned (strict security, SVG labels, dagre), token colours in light and dark, the last diagram that worked kept on an error — plus the ready blockViews entry for TextEdit and MarkdownView.

meta.whenToUse: Diagrams written as ```mermaid fences — in a TextEdit or MarkdownView (blockViews={{ mermaid: mermaidBlockView }}) or on their own (MermaidBlock, renderMermaid).
meta.whenNotToUse: Charts of data (Chart), or an image someone uploaded (FileViewer).

items.name: qr-code
items.title: QR Code
items.description: A QR code for a value, drawn as one crisp SVG path — dark modules on a light rounded tile in both themes, with the standard quiet zone — encoded on the server or the client by uqr.

meta.whenToUse: Handing a link to a phone: a scan-to-open code beside the link itself (record on your phone, open in the app, join a call).
meta.whenNotToUse: The only way to reach something — always show or copy the link too (CopyButton); a barcode or an image someone uploaded (Image).

items.name: brand-logo
items.title: Brand Logo
items.description: A provider, tool or channel's mark in a small monochrome tile — Simple Icons (CC0) glyphs in the theme's ink, or the brand's first letter where no CC0 mark exists. Server-safe.

meta.whenToUse: Naming a model provider, coding tool or channel by its mark in a list, a picker or a settings row (Anthropic, OpenAI, Slack, MCP) — beside its name, or labelled when it stands alone.
meta.whenNotToUse: A brand in its own colours or a wordmark (BrandIcon with a thesvg module); a person or workspace (Avatar); a functional icon (lucide).

items.name: reactions
items.title: Reactions
items.description: Slack-style emoji reactions: pills with counts that toggle, a hover card naming who reacted, and an add-reaction button with quick reactions.

meta.whenToUse: Letting people react to a comment, message or post with emoji.
meta.whenNotToUse: A single like or rating — use a toggle button.

items.name: aspect-ratio
items.title: Aspect Ratio
items.description: Constrains its children to a given width-to-height ratio.

meta.whenToUse: Reserve a fixed ratio for media — a video embed, a cover image, a map tile — so the layout does not shift as it loads.
meta.whenNotToUse: Content whose height must follow its text; use ordinary flow instead.

items.name: attachment
items.title: Attachment
items.description: A file chip / thumbnail card for chat, record-file and upload-queue surfaces — media slot, name + meta, idle/uploading/processing/error/done states, determinate progress, a muted tile, an actions row, a full-bleed trigger, and a scrolling, grid or dense list group, overlay action slots on a tile, a whole-tile open into the FileViewer, and a column-sized tile grid or scrolling row.

meta.whenToUse: File and media tiles on any surface: chat attachments, record files, upload queues — a chip or thumbnail with name, size, lifecycle state, determinate upload progress (AttachmentProgress), a muted tile for a file no longer in use, and remove or download actions; AttachmentGroup lays them out as a scrolling row or a grid.
meta.whenNotToUse: Acquiring files (drop, browse, paste) - that is Dropzone; Attachment renders the files after acquisition.

items.name: audio-player
items.title: Audio Player
items.description: A compact custom audio transport with play/pause, skip, seek, a tappable speed control, and keyboard shortcuts — a single line on a wide player, two lines with an optional transcript control on a narrow, mobile-width player; a floating pill variant and a global AudioPlayerProvider + useGlobalPlayer that keep one recording playing across routes.

meta.whenToUse: A single audio asset that needs a compact, branded transport with rewind/forward, a tappable speed control, keyboard shortcuts, and a two-line mobile layout with an optional transcript control; `docked` pins a closable player to the bottom of a scroll column, a function `src` resolves a signed URL on first play, `actionsRef` seeks it from a transcript or chapter list, and `peaks` draws a stored waveform without downloading the file.
meta.whenNotToUse: Playlists, queue management, waveform editing, audio recording, or a bar of bulk actions over a selection (ActionBar).

items.name: auto-save-input
items.title: Auto Save Input
items.description: An input that debounces edits and persists them via an async onSave, with an inline idle/saving/saved/error status.

meta.whenToUse: Settings-style fields that save on pause without a Save button — names, slugs, inline fields.
meta.whenNotToUse: Form submission with a Save button, secrets, or one-time codes.

items.name: avatar
items.title: Avatar
items.description: A circular user or entity image with a fallback, a badge, and an overlapping group.

meta.whenToUse: Represent a user/entity with a photo, falling back to initials — alone or stacked in a group.
meta.whenNotToUse: When you must fetch/resolve the image source — presentational; resolve R2/CDN keys app-side.

items.name: avatar-picker
items.title: Avatar Picker
items.description: A person's avatar that opens a dialog to upload, change or remove their photo — the file is staged in a 128px drop circle and saved only on Update.

meta.whenToUse: A profile or member settings row where someone sets their own photo.
meta.whenNotToUse: Attaching files to a record (Dropzone / Attachment) or picking a person (SearchableSelect).

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: A compact label or status chip — upstream's six variants plus our four status tones (COL-12).

meta.whenToUse: Label or annotate status, counts, or categories — e.g. Active, Beta, 3 New.
meta.whenNotToUse: An action — use a Button. A Badge is a label; it can be a link through render, but never a control.

items.name: board
items.title: Board
items.description: Kanban lanes — full-height lanes that scroll their cards inside, sticky headers with a collapse button left of the ⋯ menu, a subtle top-down fade on each lane, + Add after the last card (the empty lane's action when it has none), Nothing here / Drop here empty zones, per-lane skeletons and load-on-scroll paging; live pointer and touch drag (lift, make room, settle, edge auto-scroll), a keyboard pick-up/move/drop model, a per-card ⋯ menu of the card's own actions, optimistic moves with rollback and a toast, and one lane at a time on a phone.

meta.whenToUse: Cross-column card movement — pipelines, kanban, staged workflows — where the host owns ordering and the move can be refused by a server gate; lanes may be partially loaded (count shows the total) and cards may be links to their records.
meta.whenNotToUse: Single-list reordering (sortable-list), tabular data (data-list/data-grid), or static column layouts with no movement (plain Cards in a flex row).

items.name: board-card
items.title: Board Card
items.description: A work item as a board card — a round completion tick, a two-line title, a muted context line, and a bottom row with the due chip (destructive when overdue, warning when due today), the priority chip, a source icon and the assignee's avatar.

meta.whenToUse: The content of a Board card (tasks, deals, tickets) — DataList's board view renders one per row — or a standalone work-item card.
meta.whenNotToUse: A record with an image (MediaCard), a long body (Card), or a table row (DataList).

items.name: breadcrumb
items.title: Breadcrumb
items.description: A hierarchical navigation trail — links, separators, the current page, and ellipsis collapse for long paths.

meta.whenToUse: Show location in a hierarchy and navigate back up — nested pages, file trees.
meta.whenNotToUse: Primary navigation or a menu — a breadcrumb reflects location only.

items.name: breadcrumb-cascade
items.title: Breadcrumb Cascade
items.description: Two additions to a breadcrumb trail for a file browser: BreadcrumbDropTarget, a crumb that takes rows dragged from a DataList, and BreadcrumbSiblings, a menu of a segment's siblings.

meta.whenToUse: A file browser's trail: drop rows onto a parent folder's crumb, or jump to a sibling folder from a segment's menu.
meta.whenNotToUse: A plain location trail (Breadcrumb alone), or primary navigation.

items.name: bubble
items.title: Bubble
items.description: A chat speech bubble - 7 token-driven variants (incl. brand-tinted), start/end alignment, interactive content, and a floating reactions chip.

meta.whenToUse: The speech surface inside a Message - sent/received styling, reactions, interactive bubbles.
meta.whenNotToUse: Non-conversational callouts - use Alert or Card.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: Trigger an action — upstream's six variants and eight sizes, plus a loading state (API-5).

meta.whenToUse: Any clickable action — submit, confirm, destructive, etc.
meta.whenNotToUse: Navigation to a URL — style the link with buttonVariants(): <Link href className={buttonVariants({ variant, size })}>.

items.name: button-group
items.title: Button Group
items.description: Joins buttons, inputs, selects and dropdowns into one connected control group — horizontal or vertical, with a separator and a text addon.

meta.whenToUse: Join related controls into one unit — a split action, a segmented action bar, an input with a leading or trailing control.
meta.whenNotToUse: A single selection among peers (ToggleGroup) or unrelated actions that only happen to sit together.

items.name: calendar
items.title: Calendar
items.description: A date-field calendar built on react-day-picker — single, multiple and range selection, month/year dropdowns, week numbers and custom cell sizes.

meta.whenToUse: Choosing one or more dates from a month grid — a booking range, a report period, a due date inside a Popover.
meta.whenNotToUse: A free-text date a user already knows (an input with a mask) or a time-only value.

items.name: card
items.title: Card
items.description: A content surface with composable header, content, footer and action parts.

meta.whenToUse: Group related content into a bordered surface — summaries, plan tiles, settings sections.
meta.whenNotToUse: Single standalone values or page layout regions; never nest cards or add shadows.

items.name: carousel
items.title: Carousel
items.description: A slide track with previous and next controls — horizontal or vertical, any slide size or spacing, Embla options, events and plugins.

meta.whenToUse: A horizontal or vertical run of peer items the reader scrolls through one or a few at a time — a gallery, a set of feature cards, a testimonial run.
meta.whenNotToUse: Content the reader must not miss, or a list they need to scan and compare — put that in the page, not behind a control.

items.name: chart
items.title: Chart
items.description: A themed Recharts wrapper — a ChartConfig that maps each series to a colour and a label, a bordered tooltip and legend, and Recharts' own built-in keyboard + screen-reader layer.

meta.whenToUse: Visualizing series data (trends, comparisons, breakdowns) with a Line/Bar/Area/Pie/Radar chart that needs to match the design system's theme automatically in light and dark. Draw a one-series chart in --chart-single and reach for --chart-1…--chart-8 from two series up.
meta.whenNotToUse: Tabular/exact-value data a user needs to read precisely (Table), a single KPI number (a stat tile), or a progress/completion metric (Progress).

items.name: checkbox
items.title: Checkbox
items.description: A binary (or indeterminate) toggle built on Base UI Checkbox, with a 24px invisible hit area (A11Y-2).

meta.whenToUse: Toggle a single option on/off, accept terms, or drive a 'select all' parent with indeterminate.
meta.whenNotToUse: Mutually-exclusive choices (RadioGroup); instant self-saving settings (Switch).

items.name: chip
items.title: Chip
items.description: The one labelled pill primitive — 10 decorative hues, two tiers, an optional selection rung, and a real 24x24 remove control. Behind Tag and FilterChip; ComboboxChip is Base UI's own chip, not this primitive.

meta.whenToUse: A labelled, optionally removable pill — a record label, an applied filter, a selected value in a multi-select.
meta.whenNotToUse: A status signal (Badge) or a clickable action (Button); a Chip's root is not interactive.

items.name: chip-input
items.title: Chip Input
items.description: Free-token entry field — Enter/comma/paste commits chips, Backspace removes, per-chip validation marks invalid entries instead of dropping them. InputGroup field chrome + real Tag chips.

meta.whenToUse: Entering an open set of short tokens — tags, e-mail recipients, domains, webhook events — where values are typed or pasted, not picked from a finite list.
meta.whenNotToUse: Selection from a known item set (Combobox multiple), or a read-only label list (TagGroup).

items.name: code-highlight
items.title: Code Highlight
items.description: The one shared lowlight instance (highlight.js common grammars) CodeBlock loads lazily and TextEdit's code block uses — one module so the grammars stay out of the main bundle.

meta.whenToUse: Highlighting code with the design system's shared grammars.
meta.whenNotToUse: Rendering code — use CodeBlock.

items.name: code-block
items.title: Code Block
items.description: A code panel with a language header and copy affordance — the shared code surface for chat transcripts, docs, and examples.

meta.whenToUse: Fenced/source code that deserves a labelled, copyable panel.
meta.whenNotToUse: Inline code (a mono chip) or terminal output theatre (Terminal).

items.name: collapsible
items.title: Collapsible
items.description: A single toggleable open/close region with an animated height, built on Base UI Collapsible.

meta.whenToUse: A single show/hide region — extra detail, an optional form section, 'read more'.
meta.whenNotToUse: Several coordinated sections where one opens at a time — use Accordion.

items.name: color-picker
items.title: Color Picker
items.description: A swatch-triggered popover presenting a grid of preset colors — pick one, fire onValueChange, mark the selection.

meta.whenToUse: Pick a single color from a small curated set — labels, tags, calendar categories.
meta.whenNotToUse: Full-spectrum hue/saturation/alpha selection.

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.description: A filterable, keyboard-navigable listbox behind a text input — type-to-filter, grouped items, an announced empty state, and a multi-select chips mode.

meta.whenToUse: Choosing from a large or dynamic set that benefits from typing to narrow it down — searchable pickers, tag/label multi-select, async-loaded results. A two-line option composes ItemTitle + ItemDescription, and the description is the option's accessible description.
meta.whenNotToUse: A small, fixed set with no need to search (Select), boolean on/off (Switch), or a few always-visible options (radios/checkboxes).

items.name: command
items.title: Command Menu
items.description: A searchable command palette — filtered, grouped items with keyboard navigation, optionally inside a ⌘K dialog.

meta.whenToUse: A keyboard-first command palette — global ⌘K, action launchers, a filtered list of things to do or go to — including a large palette over server results, with a loading status, two-line results and a footer of key hints.
meta.whenNotToUse: Picking a form value, and never a multi-select — Command's check mark is visual only (Select, SearchableSelect or Combobox) — or a small static action menu (DropdownMenu).

items.name: context-menu
items.title: Context Menu
items.description: The same menu vocabulary opened by right-click, positioned at the pointer.

meta.whenToUse: Secondary actions on an object the user has already found — a file row, a canvas node, a board card. A two-line row composes ItemTitle + ItemDescription, and the description is the row's accessible description — including a disabled row's reason.
meta.whenNotToUse: The only way to reach an action — right-click is discoverable by almost nobody; pair it with a visible menu.

items.name: copy-button
items.title: Copy Button
items.description: Copy a value to the clipboard with transient check feedback — icon-only by default, with an optional visible status label.

meta.whenToUse: Copy a short opaque value — API key, invite link, ID, snippet — with clear confirmation.
meta.whenNotToUse: Long-form content to read/edit, or when there is no discrete value to copy.

items.name: data-grid
items.title: Data Grid
items.description: The full-parity grid — client or host-sorted multi-key sort, frozen, resizable and windowed columns, header reorder, client or host grouping flattened into the row virtualiser, a summary row, cursor paging, an APG grid keyboard layer with inline cell editing, and an embedded mode for a table block in a page (sized to its rows, read-only for viewers).

meta.whenToUse: Record tables that need grouping, inline cell editing, multi-key sort, column management, frozen or resizable columns, or 10k+ rows and 100+ columns via row and column virtualization — the CRM pipeline-table and spreadsheet tier.
meta.whenNotToUse: Simple presentational record lists — DataList is lighter and still the right default; kanban views (Board).

items.name: floating-cell-editor
items.title: Floating Cell Editor
items.description: A cell's editor that opens over the cell instead of inside it — anchored at the cell's rect, a little wider and taller than it, with a lock layer that takes presses and scroll behind it while pinch-zoom still passes.

meta.whenToUse: An editor too big for its cell (a long text, a picker, a date) that should open over the cell and keep the cell's own face visible; DataGrid uses it for `editing="floating"`.
meta.whenNotToUse: A pop-up that is not tied to a cell (Popover), or an editor that fits the cell (EditableCell inline).

items.name: dropdown-menu-form
items.title: Dropdown Menu Form
items.description: The parts a DropdownMenu needs to hold a small form — a text input that keeps its keys, a switch row with a hint, and a menu that opens at a point instead of under a trigger.

meta.whenToUse: A menu that carries an input, a setting switch, or opens where the pointer was (a column header's field menu).
meta.whenNotToUse: A form of several fields (a Popover or a Dialog with Field).

items.name: option-list-editor
items.title: Option List Editor
items.description: Edits a choice field's options as rows — a hue, a name, remove, and add — holding no state of its own, with a change per keystroke and a commit when an edit is done.

meta.whenToUse: Defining the options of a single- or multiple-choice field, in a panel or in a menu.
meta.whenNotToUse: Choosing among existing options (SearchableSelect, ChipInput).

items.name: block-header
items.title: Block Header
items.description: A live block's header row in a page — icon · title · controls (View ▾, Filter) · ⋯ · ↗ Open — with an empty state that hosts the source picker ("Pick a table…").

meta.whenToUse: The top row of a block that shows records from elsewhere inside a page — a table view (DataGrid embedded's toolbar), a task list — and the block's unconfigured state with its picker.
meta.whenNotToUse: A page's own header (DocumentLayoutHeader), a section heading (DocumentLayoutSection), or a record's header.

items.name: data-list
items.title: Data List
items.description: A generic, typed data table — configurable columns, row selection (shift ranges, ⌘/Ctrl+A, Esc, a selection ActionBar), sortable columns (indicator, custom compare and first direction, client or manual), a standard rowActions ⋯ column always last, untinted-link rows (no underline), loading, Empty-based emptyState and noResults states, and rows that drag into folders and breadcrumbs.

meta.whenToUse: A list of records as a table, a card grid or board lanes (view) with typed columns, selection, click-to-sort, loading/empty states, keyset paging through loadMore, rows as links, sections, thumbnails and a row-actions column.
meta.whenNotToUse: Full-parity grids with grouping/editing/virtualization (DataGrid), or a simple static table (Table).

items.name: data-list-skeleton
items.title: Data List Skeleton
items.description: A DataList and its ListToolbar while they load, in the list's own geometry (table rows or grid cards), without loading the list.

meta.whenToUse: A route's or Suspense fallback's loading state for a DataList page (rows, grid cards, the toolbar).
meta.whenNotToUse: DataList's own `loading` (a list already on screen refetching).

items.name: data-list-pager
items.title: Data List Pager
items.description: A controlled paging footer for DataList — a tabular-numeral range summary, a rows-per-page Select, and a windowed Pagination that hides on a single page.

meta.whenToUse: Paging a DataList (or any host-paged list) in place: the range, an optional rows-per-page chooser (omit onPageSizeChange for a fixed size), and page buttons in its footer slot, with page state owned by the host.
meta.whenNotToUse: Keyset or cursor paging with no total (LoadMore, or DataList's and DataGrid's loadMore), or bare page links with no page-size choice (Pagination).

items.name: cursor-pager
items.title: Cursor Pager
items.description: Previous and Next for keyset (cursor) paging — a range label and two buttons, with no page numbers and no total.

meta.whenToUse: Keyset-paged lists that page instead of scroll — DataGrid's pagedMode, or any host that keeps a cursor history and knows only whether a previous and a next page exist.
meta.whenNotToUse: Lists with a total and page numbers (DataListPager), or continuous paging on scroll (LoadMore).

items.name: load-more
items.title: Load More
items.description: The shared Load more footer for keyset lists — an outline button that keeps its width while loading, an error line with Try again, and an optional end caption.

meta.whenToUse: The footer of a keyset (cursor) list — DataList's or DataGrid's loadMore, a board lane, a feed: load the next batch, retry a failed one, optionally say the list has ended.
meta.whenNotToUse: Numbered pages with a known total (DataListPager); loading on scroll with no button.

items.name: media-card
items.title: Media Card
items.description: A record as a card — an image, the title, a meta line, a badge and a ⋯ menu — where the whole card is one link.

meta.whenToUse: A card per record in a grid (DataList view="grid" renders one per row), or card content on a board.
meta.whenNotToUse: A record with a long body or its own controls (Card), or a row in a table (DataList).

items.name: thumbnail
items.title: Thumbnail
items.description: A small rounded, cover-fit image, 32 or 48px, with a fallback for records that have no image.

meta.whenToUse: A record image in a list row (32px) or a card (48px), with the app mark as the fallback.
meta.whenNotToUse: A person (Avatar), a large image or media (Image), or an icon (Icon).

items.name: view-tabs
items.title: View Tabs
items.description: A table's saved views as a tab row: shared views, a divider, then the reader's own; a lock on locked views; a + menu for a grid or board view, shared or personal; the open view's actions; one Select below a narrow container.

meta.whenToUse: Switching between saved views of one table or list (grid and board views, shared and personal).
meta.whenNotToUse: A layout switch between a list and a card grid of the same data (ListToolbar's Layout tool), or page sections (Tabs).

items.name: use-overflow-fold
items.title: useOverflowFold
items.description: Measured fold — decide whether a row (tabs, saved views) fits the room it is given, and fold it into one control when it does not, with hysteresis so it never flickers.

meta.whenToUse: A row that should become one dropdown when it does not fit its container — scope tabs, route tabs, saved views.
meta.whenNotToUse: Truncating one piece of text (useOverflow, TruncatedText) or a layout CSS container queries can express.

items.name: list-toolbar
items.title: List Toolbar
items.description: The one header row of every list and table: the search left, the icon tools (Filter · Sort · Layout · Display · ⋯) right; scope tabs in their own row above and the filter row under it. Measures its own width and collapses in a fixed order.

meta.whenToUse: Above any list, table or board page — scope tabs (their own row), search, filter, sort, layout, display options and view actions. The page's main button is not here: it sits at the right end of the app's top bar.
meta.whenNotToUse: A form's own controls, a record page's header actions (PageHeader), or a picker's inline search (SearchInput).

items.name: filter-row
items.title: Filter Row
items.description: The chips under a ListToolbar: + Filter, pinned facets (ListFacet, PeopleFacet, DateRangeFilter — dashed while unset), the other chips, Clear — and after an AI filter run, one line with what it added, Undo and what it could not match.

meta.whenToUse: The filters a ListToolbar's Filter tool opens: facets, applied chips, the AI note.
meta.whenNotToUse: A single search box, or a condition builder (FilterBuilder in a dialog).

items.name: add-filter-menu
items.title: Add Filter Menu
items.description: + Filter: one input (“Filter by…”) that narrows the field list and, when the page passes an AI filter and the text reads as a phrase, offers “Filter with AI” first; fields drill into their value pickers in the same popover.

meta.whenToUse: Adding a filter to a FilterRow — by field or, with the page's AI filter, in plain language.
meta.whenNotToUse: Choosing a value for one known field (a facet), or a free-text search (SearchInput).

items.name: sort-menu
items.title: Sort Menu
items.description: The one-key sort: the fields, then the two directions worded by field type (Oldest first, A → Z, Low → high), with Reset while not at the page default.

meta.whenToUse: Sorting a list by one key from the ListToolbar's Sort tool.
meta.whenNotToUse: Several sort keys at once (SortBuilder), or a column header's own sort.

items.name: display-menu
items.title: Display Menu
items.description: The toolbar's Display tool: Layout and Sort once folded in, row height, group by, a Columns drill-in, the Show switches (archived, closed, subtasks) and Reset — one surface, no fills.

meta.whenToUse: How a list's rows look and which lifecycle states it includes, from a ListToolbar.
meta.whenNotToUse: Actions on the view (ListToolbarMenu), or filters on rows (FilterRow).

items.name: data-table-parts
items.title: Data Table Parts
items.description: The chrome DataList and DataGrid share — sort header, selection cells, skeleton rows, the empty row, the column resize handle, the summary cell, column class rules, and the selection/sort/controlled-state hooks.

meta.whenToUse: Installed automatically with DataList or DataGrid; import it directly when building a bespoke table that should share their sort header, selection cells and column rules.
meta.whenNotToUse: A plain presentational table (Table alone), or as a table component in its own right — these are parts, not a renderer.

items.name: date-picker
items.title: Date Picker
items.description: Pick a single date, a date and a time, or a date range from a calendar popover — token-styled, keyboard-navigable, with optional quick presets.

meta.whenToUse: Selecting a single date, a date with a time of day (DateTimePicker: the calendar and the time in one popup, on the reader's clock), or a range (with optional Today/Last-7-days presets) from a popover. size="sm" + variant="ghost" is the inline row tier; clearable adds a clear control that returns focus to the trigger.
meta.whenNotToUse: Free-form/partial dates (masked Input) or inline-only calendars (use Calendar directly).

items.name: time-field
items.title: Time Field
items.description: A time of day as one typed field: "HH:mm" in and out, shown on the locale's 12- or 24-hour clock, stepped by the arrow keys within min and max.

meta.whenToUse: A time of day on its own: a schedule's time, a reminder, opening hours. Typed ("930", "9:30 pm") or stepped with the arrow keys; the value is always HH:mm.
meta.whenNotToUse: A date and a time together (DateTimePicker), a duration (NumberField with a unit), or an instant across time zones.

items.name: recurrence-picker
items.title: Recurrence Picker
items.description: The body of a repeat popover: presets, a custom editor (every n days, weeks, months or years; weekdays; month day; ends; time) and the host's preview of the next dates. Never computes a date.

meta.whenToUse: Choosing how something repeats — a Repeat property, a schedule, a reminder — inside the host's popover or ResponsiveDialog, with presets built from the record's date and the host's formatted next dates.
meta.whenNotToUse: Picking one date (DatePicker) or a time alone (TimeField); computing occurrences (the host's RRULE engine).

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: A modal overlay — backdrop, centred popup, a plain right-aligned footer and an optional close button; opens onto the first field or the popup, never the close ×.

meta.whenToUse: Modal interactions requiring full attention — confirmations, focused forms, destructive-action prompts. size sm/default/lg/xl steps the width; put long content in DialogBody so the header and footer stay in view.
meta.whenNotToUse: Non-blocking feedback (Toast), inline contextual content (Popover/Tooltip), or a swipeable bottom panel (Drawer).

items.name: direction
items.title: Direction
items.description: Base UI's DirectionProvider and useDirection — the text-direction context every component reads for its logical-property layout.

meta.whenToUse: Rendering a right-to-left subtree, or reading the active direction inside a component.
meta.whenNotToUse: Setting the document direction — that is the `dir` attribute on <html>.

items.name: date-time
items.title: Date Time
items.description: The one Intl-based dates & times module — formatRelative, formatDuration, formatDate, formatDateTime, formatDateRange, formatTimeOfDay, formatDueLabel, groupByDay, and the tz cookie + getTimeZone server helper. Plain functions for server and client.

meta.whenToUse: Any date, time, duration, due label or day grouping shown as text — on the server, in route handlers, emails or client code.
meta.whenNotToUse: API/JSON output — keep ISO strings there.

items.name: grid-clipboard
items.title: Grid Clipboard
items.description: The spreadsheet clipboard as data: parse TSV, clipboard HTML and Google Sheets' typed values into a cell matrix; write TSV and HTML for a copied range; fit a paste to a selected range.

meta.whenToUse: Copy and paste between a grid and spreadsheets (Excel, Google Sheets, Numbers, Airtable) — DataGrid's cells mode, or a host's own paste preview or import.
meta.whenNotToUse: CSV files (a CSV parser), or rich text paste into an editor.

items.name: drag-item
items.title: Drag Item
items.description: The one visual recipe for a use-drag-reorder item — drop-edge hairlines on all four edges, the lift dim, and the pending shimmer — shared by Board and SortableList instead of copied into each.

meta.whenToUse: Building a drag surface on use-drag-reorder — spread it onto the element carrying the hook`s getItemProps() attributes.
meta.whenNotToUse: File drag-in (use-file-drop) or any surface that does not use the reorder hook.

items.name: markdown-as-typed
items.title: Markdown As Typed
items.description: Stored Markdown as the person typed it — markdownAsTyped keeps real formatting, drops the escapes the writer added only to keep plain text from reading as syntax (\_\_init\_\_ → __init__), turns hard breaks into newlines, and keeps code byte for byte. Pure strings, server-safe.

meta.whenToUse: Handing a person's stored message to a reader that isn't a Markdown renderer: a model's input, a chat bubble, a plain-text notification.
meta.whenNotToUse: Anything parsed back into an editor — keep the stored Markdown, which round-trips.

items.name: text-anchor
items.title: Text Anchor
items.description: Where a comment sits in a text, stored so it survives edits — TextAnchor (offsets, quote, 80 characters of context each side), anchorFromRange and resolveAnchor (offsets → context → unique quote → orphaned). Pure strings, server-safe.

meta.whenToUse: Storing and re-finding comment anchors on a text — on the server (a save route) or in the client, with TextEdit's annotations.
meta.whenNotToUse: Positions inside a live ProseMirror document — convert with text-anchor-doc first.

items.name: text-anchor-doc
items.title: Text Anchor Doc
items.description: The bridge between a ProseMirror document and comment-anchor offsets — anchorText (blocks joined by a newline, a mention as @label, other leaves as ￼), textIndex, and the exact two-way offsetsToRange / rangeToOffsets map.

meta.whenToUse: Mapping comment anchors onto a TextEdit (Tiptap/ProseMirror) document and back.
meta.whenNotToUse: Server code with no ProseMirror document — use text-anchor on the flat text.

items.name: text-edit-grammar
items.title: Text Edit Grammar
items.description: VegaStack Markdown v1 beyond CommonMark + GFM, as plain strings — mention links (parse, write, SQL twin), callout markers, toggles, media blocks, image widths, fence info and heading ids. No dependencies; server-safe.

meta.whenToUse: Reading or writing the Markdown constructs TextEdit stores — mentions, callouts, toggles, media, image widths — on a server or in a light renderer.
meta.whenNotToUse: Parsing a whole document — use text-edit-markdown.

items.name: embed-providers
items.title: Embed Providers
items.description: The video hosts a document may embed — YouTube and Loom: matchEmbed reads a URL's provider and video id (YouTube's start time too), each provider rebuilds its player src from the id alone, and EMBED_FRAME_ORIGINS is the frame-src allowlist. Pure, server-safe.

meta.whenToUse: Deciding whether a URL is an embeddable video (YouTube, Loom) and building its player src — in TextEdit, MarkdownView, a server import, or a Content-Security-Policy's frame-src.
meta.whenNotToUse: Any other host: the allowlist is the security boundary; add a provider here, never a raw URL as a frame src.

items.name: text-edit-schema
items.title: Text Edit Schema
items.description: TextEdit’s document schema as plain Tiptap extensions — every node, mark and attribute with its VegaStack Markdown rules, stable block ids (`blockId`) that Markdown never carries. No React, no DOM: the editor adds node views, a server builds the identical schema.

meta.whenToUse: Building a TextEdit document anywhere — a collaboration server, an import, an API — with exactly the editor’s nodes and attributes.
meta.whenNotToUse: Rendering a document to read — use MarkdownView.

items.name: text-edit-markdown
items.title: Text Edit Markdown
items.description: VegaStack Markdown v1 in and out of a TextEdit document, identical in a browser and on a server — markdownToDoc, docToMarkdown, normalizeMarkdown, docToText, an isolated marked instance, minimal escaping, raw HTML as text, and the editor’s VegaStackMarkdown extension.

meta.whenToUse: Converting between Markdown and a TextEdit document on a server — import, export, search text, a collaboration server’s read copy.
meta.whenNotToUse: Rendering Markdown to read — use MarkdownView.

items.name: file-kind
items.title: File Kind
items.description: The one answer to "what is this file and how big is it" — formatBytes (1024 base, one decimal under 10), fileKindOf (MIME first, extension fallback, 25 kinds from images and PDFs to CAD, photometric and design files) and FileTypeIcon/FileKindTile (the lucide icon, tint and label per kind) — shared by Attachment rows, FileViewer, UploadPanel, AvatarPicker and FolderTree.

meta.whenToUse: Any file surface that shows a size, picks an icon for a file, or branches on what kind of file it holds.
meta.whenNotToUse: Previewing a file (FileViewer) or acquiring one (use-file-drop).

items.name: upload-progress
items.title: Upload Progress
items.description: The arithmetic behind an upload time left: createRateEstimator (an EWMA of acknowledged bytes over 1 s ticks that ignores the first 3 s, reports after 5 s and 2%, and moves only on a 15% change), formatTimeLeft ("About 2 minutes left") and formatBytesProgress ("2.1 MB of 3.4 MB").

meta.whenToUse: An upload engine or surface that shows speed, time left, or bytes done of a total.
meta.whenNotToUse: Formatting a single size (formatBytes in file-kind) or a download progress you do not control.

items.name: media-probe
items.title: Media Probe
items.description: Upload-time reads in the browser, dependency-free — probeVideo (duration, size and a JPEG poster frame via video + canvas), probeAudio (duration and up to 200 waveform peaks via OfflineAudioContext, skipped over 50 MB) and extractPptxThumbnail (an Office file's docProps/thumbnail.jpeg via a zip central-directory reader and DecompressionStream).

meta.whenToUse: An upload flow that stores a video's poster and duration, an audio file's waveform peaks, or an Office file's preview picture beside the original, so grids, players and FileViewer show them without re-reading the file.
meta.whenNotToUse: Server code (it needs a browser), or parsing Office content (a sheet or a slide) — that is the app's parser, returned through FileViewer's loadPreview.

items.name: page-layout
items.title: Page Layout
items.description: The page-width contract — the prose/form/default/full vocabulary ShellPage takes, and definePageWidths, one route → width map that a page, its loading skeleton and a test all read.

meta.whenToUse: Choosing how wide a page is — declare every route's width once with definePageWidths and read it from the page's ShellPage, its loading skeleton and a route test.
meta.whenNotToUse: A page outside the Shell (sign-in, a marketing page) — it owns its own layout.

items.name: tile-overlay
items.title: Tile Overlay
items.description: The one visual recipe for media tiles — the photo scrim, the blurred-scrim overlay button, the top-left and top-right overlay slots that show on hover or focus, and the responsive at-most-N-per-row tile grid — shared by Attachment, SortableList and AvatarPicker.

meta.whenToUse: Building a tile surface with controls over an image — spread tileCornerClasses on the slot, tileOverlayButtonClasses on a ghost icon Button, tileGroupClass on the tile.
meta.whenNotToUse: Chrome that does not sit over media — use a plain Button.

items.name: disclosure-trigger
items.title: Disclosure Trigger
items.description: The one class recipe for a ghost Button that expands a section in place — clears the popup-open grey that aria-expanded paints, so an open section never looks pressed — shared by RecordAsideSection, SectionToggle, AgentPanel and ShareDialog.

meta.whenToUse: A ghost Button that is a CollapsibleTrigger or otherwise toggles a section open in place — put disclosureTriggerClasses in its className.
meta.whenNotToUse: A trigger that opens a popup (menu, popover, select) — there the aria-expanded grey is the right cue.

items.name: drawer
items.title: Drawer
items.description: A swipeable panel with snap points — four directions, a swipe handle, nesting, and a non-modal mode.

meta.whenToUse: A touch-first panel the user drags — a mobile action sheet, a half-height detail panel, a stack of nested steps.
meta.whenNotToUse: A desktop side panel with no gesture (Sheet), or a centred modal (Dialog).

items.name: dropdown-menu
items.title: Dropdown Menu
items.description: An anchored action menu — items, submenus, checkboxes, radio groups, shortcuts and a destructive variant.

meta.whenToUse: A list of actions or option toggles anchored to a button — row actions, an account menu, a view switcher. A two-line row composes ItemTitle + ItemDescription, and the description is the row's accessible description — including a disabled row's reason.
meta.whenNotToUse: Choosing a form value (Select), navigating between pages (NavigationMenu), or content the user reads (Popover).

items.name: dropzone
items.title: Dropzone
items.description: File acquisition surface — drop, click-to-browse, and paste — as a thin shell over use-file-drop; the surface is the named focusable control over a hidden picker-bridge input; data-dragging/data-drag-invalid styling flags.

meta.whenToUse: A visible upload surface — drop files, click to browse, paste — that hands accepted File[]s to the host and typed rejections back.
meta.whenNotToUse: Chrome-less acquisition inside another surface (compose use-file-drop directly) or rendering the staged files and their upload progress (Attachment with AttachmentProgress, laid out by AttachmentGroup).

items.name: upload-panel
items.title: Upload Panel
items.description: The uploads card pinned bottom-end: a header naming the batch with time left, file and folder rows with progress rings, failures with Retry, interrupted rows with Choose file and destination links, a done card that dismisses itself, a confirm before cancelling, and a bottom sheet on phones. Controlled; the host engine uploads.

meta.whenToUse: Showing every upload in flight across the app — files and folders, progress, time left, failures and where each one lands — from the app shell, so uploads survive navigation.
meta.whenNotToUse: Choosing files (Dropzone), an attachment inside a composer (Attachment), or a one-off short save (a toast).

items.name: editable-cell
items.title: Editable Cell
items.description: Inline-editable value whose edit mode looks like view — same box, inherited type, no border — with optimistic saves, a delayed spinner, rollback plus a Retry toast on failure, required, multiline, table-cell and heading variants, and a typed text/select/custom editor registry.

meta.whenToUse: Any optimistic inline edit of a single value — grid cells (focusMode=managed), record-page property lists, settings rows — where the write is async and can fail.
meta.whenNotToUse: Debounced save-as-you-type on a standing form field (AutoSaveInput), or whole forms (Field).

items.name: field-cell
items.title: Field Cell
items.description: One display and one editor per field type — text, long text, number, currency, percent, date, date-time, choices, checkbox, person, link, file, URL, email, phone and the read-only computed types — for a grid cell (FieldCellEditor), a panel or a form (FieldInput), shown the same everywhere (FieldCellDisplay).

meta.whenToUse: Showing or editing a typed field value — a table's cells, a row panel, a record page's custom fields — so every surface shows and edits a type the same way.
meta.whenNotToUse: A single untyped inline edit (EditableCell), or a form field with its own validation and layout (Field + the control).

items.name: emoji-picker
items.title: Emoji Picker
items.description: A popover with a quick row, search, a category bar, recents and a category-grouped grid of emoji that returns the selected character via onValueChange (curated set, loaded lazily).

meta.whenToUse: Lightweight emoji insertion — reactions, comments, status, icon selection.
meta.whenNotToUse: A complete Unicode emoji browser — extend the embedded set or use a library.

items.name: panel-search
items.title: Panel Search
items.description: The sticky, box-free search row a filtering popup puts at the top of its panel (decision OVL-11) — shared by EmojiPicker and ShortcutOverlay.

meta.whenToUse: Installed automatically with EmojiPicker or ShortcutOverlay; import it directly when building another popup that filters its own contents.
meta.whenNotToUse: A standalone search field on a page — that is Input, or InputGroup with a leading addon. A command palette is Command, which brings its own input.

items.name: suggestion-menu
items.title: Suggestion Menu
items.description: The caret-anchored list an editor opens while you type a trigger (@, /, {{) — shared by TextEdit's slash and mention menus and TemplateEditor's placeholder picker, with rows that read exactly like ComboboxItem's.

meta.whenToUse: Installed automatically with TextEdit or TemplateEditor; import it directly when another editor that keeps focus needs a caret-anchored list of suggestions.
meta.whenNotToUse: A list that takes focus or hangs off a trigger element — that is Combobox, Command or DropdownMenu.

items.name: empty
items.title: Empty
items.description: A zero-data placeholder — always an icon (the icon prop, Inbox by default), title, description and a content slot, with a compact sm size for inline empties. The one empty-state markup: DataList's emptyState and noResults (SearchX, "No matches", Clear filters) are built on it.

meta.whenToUse: When a list, table, or panel has no content — communicate the zero state and offer the next action.
meta.whenNotToUse: While loading (skeleton/spinner) or for transient post-action feedback (toast).

items.name: field
items.title: Field
items.description: The form-field scaffold — label, description, error, legend, separator and choice-card layouts in vertical, horizontal or responsive orientation.

meta.whenToUse: Wrap any form control to give it a label, description and error message: inside a Field the control gets its label, aria-describedby ids and aria-invalid from Base UI Field with no ids to wire.
meta.whenNotToUse: A bare control with its own label already wired — Field is for the label+message+a11y scaffold.

items.name: field-grid
items.title: Field Grid
items.description: A responsive one-to-three column grid of Fields by container width, plus FieldChoices: radios or checkboxes in a wrapping row.

meta.whenToUse: Forms with many short fields (specifications, settings) and short choice sets that read better side by side.
meta.whenNotToUse: A single-column dialog form (FieldGroup) or label/value read-only details (PropertyList).

items.name: filter-bar-managed
items.title: Filter Builder
items.description: The controlled nested and/or filter builder — host-injected field grammar (vocabulary + per-type value editors), depth and condition caps, focus-managed removal, and a removable FilterChip summary; plus SortBuilder, GroupByPicker and date, person, checkbox and link value editors.

meta.whenToUse: Editing a filter or a rule as data: nested and/or groups, or flat condition rules (allowGroups={false}) with a sentence summary, host-injected fields and typed value editors.
meta.whenNotToUse: A presentational chip row over host-owned filter state (filter-bar), or free-text search (Input in a toolbar).

items.name: emoji-data
items.title: Emoji Data
items.description: The curated emoji set behind EmojiPicker and Reactions, in nine categories, plus a lookup by character and a search matcher. Pure data, loaded lazily by the picker.

meta.whenToUse: Resolving an emoji's name or searching the curated set outside the picker.
meta.whenNotToUse: The full Unicode set — bring a dedicated library.

items.name: hover-card
items.title: Hover Card
items.description: A preview surface that opens on hover or focus, with configurable delays and sides.

meta.whenToUse: A non-essential preview of what a link points at — a profile, a repository, a document card.
meta.whenNotToUse: Essential content or anything a touch user must reach — hover is not available there.
